TF-IDF re-weights the count matrix
Distinctive terms (frequent in one document, rare across the corpus) get the highest weight.

From raw counts to TF-IDF
▸Plain BOW counts are dominated by the most common words, which carry little information
▸TF-IDF = term frequency × inverse document frequency, same vector length, reweighted values
▸IDF down-weights a term by how many documents it appears in, common terms count for less

TF-IDF, precisely
▸Term frequency: TF(i, d) = count(i, d) / (total words in d) [share of word i in document d]
▸Inverse document frequency: IDF(i, D) = log( NumDocs / |{d : i ∈d}| )
▸Combine: TF-IDF(i, d) = TF(i, d) · IDF(i, D)
▸A word frequent in one document but rare across the corpus scores highest
